# The committed badge satisfies EVERY acceptance criterion in PRD.md and still
# violates the Design Contract in TECH_PLAN.md. That separation is the whole
# point: a verify that only checks acceptance criteria passes this milestone,
# and only a verify that runs the contract checks can fail it.
#
# Violations planted, in contract-severity order:
#   Critical — .badge--error uses #9a9a9a text on #ffffff: 2.81:1, under the
#              contract's 4.5:1 body-text floor (SC 1.4.3, AA). The ok and warn
#              variants are 8.15:1 and 7.38:1, so the failure is isolated to
#              one variant and cannot be mistaken for a broken palette.
#   Critical — .badge--error declares a background only. The Token Contract
#              requires every semantic to declare bg, border AND text.
#   Polish   — padding of 14px and 7px are off the declared 8pt scale
#              (4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32).
#   Polish   — border-radius 5px, not the contract's committed 8px.
#
# Both tasks are [x] (done, unverified). A rigorous verify must refuse to flip
# them to [v] and must add a follow-up. A verify that skips contract checks
# flips them, because nothing in PRD.md is broken.
== file: badge.js
const LABELS = { ok: 'Healthy', warn: 'Degraded', error: 'Failed' }

function renderBadge(status) {
  const label = LABELS[status]
  if (!label) throw new Error('unknown status: ' + status)
  return '<span class="badge badge--' + status + '">' + label + '</span>'
}

module.exports = { renderBadge }
